findings.evidence: Diff defines `mulEquivOfHomeomorph_apply` (`@[simp]`) but no symm counterpart; `mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq` has both `mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq_apply` and `mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq_symm_apply`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem mulEquivOfHomeomorph_symm_apply (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X) (q : FundamentalGroup Y (e x)) : (mulEquivOfHomeomorph e x).symm q = mapOfEq ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_apply x) q := rfl`.
findings.issue: `mulEquivOfHomeomorph` gets only a `@[simp] mulEquivOfHomeomorph_apply`; there is no `mulEquivOfHomeomorph_symm_apply`. `mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq` supplies both directions (lines 108, 116), so the inverse transport across `mulEquivOfHomeomorph e x` (needed to pull a computation from Y back to X, e.g. the circle via `AddCircle.homeomorphCircle`) cannot be simplified to `mapOfEq ⟨e.symm, _⟩ _`: `mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq_symm_apply` does not fire on `(mulEquivOfHomeomorph e x).symm q` since `mulEquivOfHomeomorph` is not a simp-unfolded wrapper.

findings.evidence: Line 78 `theorem mapOfEq_id ... = p` has no attribute; the `_apply` lemmas below are annotated `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Tag `mapOfEq_id` with `@[simp]` (it is a terminating rewrite to `p`).
findings.issue: `mapOfEq_id` puts `mapOfEq (ContinuousMap.id X) h p` into normal form `p` but carries no `@[simp]`, so this reduction never fires automatically even though it is the identity-law normal form for Mathlib's `mapOfEq`.

summary: The characteristic API is nearly complete and correctly annotated, but the derived `mulEquivOfHomeomorph` lacks the `_symm_apply` lemma its sibling `mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq` provides, leaving the backward transport unsimplifiable.
